title: Finite root quotients of p-independent elements are fields
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-field], and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in k$, where $r\geq0$. Put $k^p=\{a^p:a\in k\}$. Assume the monomials $\prod_{i=1}^r b_i^{e_i}$ with $0\leq e_i<p$ are linearly independent over $k^p$. For every integer $n\geq1$, the commutative $k$-algebra $$C_n=k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]/(T_1^{p^n}-b_1,\ldots,T_r^{p^n}-b_r)$$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is a field. The classes of $\prod_iT_i^{e_i}$ with $0\leq e_i<p^n$ form a $k$-basis of $C_n$, and every $z\in C_n$ satisfies $z^{p^n}\in k$ under the canonical inclusion. For $r=0$ this means $C_n=k$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation paragraph: the residue fields of the finite root algebras in the displayed construction

proof.text: Put $q=p^n>0$ and write $t_i$ for the class of $T_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-simultaneous-root-algebra-api] with $R=k$, exponent $q$, and tuple $(b_i)$. It gives the asserted $k$-basis $t^E$, $0\leq E_i<q$, including $t^0=1$. Hence $k\to C_n$ is injective: the basis coefficient of $a\cdot1$ at $E=0$ is $a$. In particular $0\ne1$ in $C_n$. The same node identifies the empty-tuple quotient with $k$, proving the stated $r=0$ convention.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof p-base preparation paragraph; explicit finite-stage algebra argument, step 1

proof.text: Since $p\cdot1=0$ in $k$, it is also zero in its quotient algebra $C_n$. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $x\mapsto x^q$ is a ring endomorphism of $C_n$. For the unique basis expansion $z=\sum_E a_Et^E$, the defining relations $t_i^q=b_i$ therefore give $$z^q=\sum_E a_E^q\prod_i(t_i^q)^{E_i}=\sum_E a_E^q b^E.$$ The right side is the image of a scalar $c\in k$. This proves the power-in-$k$ assertion for every $z$, including zero.
